correctness.rationale: The primary source defines accelerated first-return edges, with each edge here assigned unit cost despite variable labels. Its adjacency matrices are row-source, column-target in right-to-left lexicographic order; Corollary 4.8 and Example 4.9 give the stated two permutation recursions and check the orientation. Both base maps swap the two vertices. In the independent packed BFS, each target stores a source bitset, initially the diagonal pair; unioning the frontier bitsets at the two predecessors and removing already visited bits gives exactly the pairs newly reached at each distance. A source's last discovery depth is its outward eccentricity. All sources reach all targets. A separate ordinary directed BFS cross-checks levels 1–9. I compared the saved independent results against the actual frozen census.tsv: all 174 distance bins, 15 radii, 15 diameters, 15 eccentricity histograms and 15 ordered diametral-pair counts match. In particular, levels 9–15 have d=n+4, and level 15 has radius 18, diameter 19, eccentricity counts 18:19720 and 19:13048, and 17,136 ordered diametral pairs out of 1,073,741,824 total pairs. The Moore comparison is valid because distance at most n−1 reaches no more than 2^n−1 vertices with two outgoing edges per vertex. The proof claims neither an all-level upper bound nor a bound on the unaccelerated shift time.
residual_risks: The frozen executables were not run. The independent computation verifies all histogram buckets and their statistics for the stated finite range only.

value.rationale: The accelerated graphs arise in an established proof about the Kolakoski shift; their directed metric quantifies how far apart targets remain after acceleration, beyond the qualitative fact of strong connectivity. The profile gives reusable exact benchmarks for tight diameter or eccentricity estimates. A full initial range through level 15 covers both the lower-level transitions and the seven-level diameter excess of four, while histograms measure the rarity of extreme paths rather than only their existence. This is a useful finite result, not evidence of a proved asymptotic pattern or any elapsed-shift-time bound.
residual_risks: The cutoff is finite; no stabilization or upper bound for levels beyond 15 is proved.
